key_big: Condensation joins monomers; hydrolysis splits them.
key_sub: n monomers in a chain make n − 1 bonds and release n − 1 water molecules.
body_html:
How to think about it

Large biological molecules are polymers built from monomers by condensation reactions, which release water; hydrolysis uses water to split them. Glucose makes starch, glycogen and cellulose (glycosidic bonds), amino acids make proteins (peptide bonds), and nucleotides make DNA and RNA (phosphodiester bonds).

In DNA, A pairs with T and G with C, so %A = %T and %G = %C. Enzymes lower the activation energy; their active site is complementary to the substrate and can be denatured by heat or pH.

Example

A chain of 6 glucose molecules: how many water molecules were released?

6 monomers make 5 bonds

Answer: 5

Example

DNA has 30% adenine. %G?

A + T = 60%

G + C = 40%

Answer: 20%

Common mistakes

  • Counting n instead of n − 1 bonds.
  • Pairing A with G in DNA.
  • Thinking enzymes are used up.

faq.q: What is the difference between condensation and hydrolysis?
faq.a: Condensation joins two molecules and releases water; hydrolysis breaks a bond using water.

faq.q: How do you test for a reducing sugar?
faq.a: Heat with Benedict's reagent: a colour change from blue to green, yellow, orange or brick-red shows reducing sugar.
